subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)

intro: Test. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: How many oxygen molecules are made per glucose molecule?
Which layer has the most chloroplasts?
questions.a: B) Palisade mesophyll. Palisade cells sit near the top where light is strongest.
B) Barium sulfate. Barium is an exception for sulfates.

questions.q: A glowing splint relights. The gas is...
A car brakes to a stop. Its kinetic energy goes mainly to...
options: Thermal store of brakes and surroundings
questions.a: B) Thermal store of brakes and surroundings. Friction heats the brakes; energy is conserved.

questions.q: Why is a fridge's freezer compartment at the top?
options: Cold air sinks, setting up a convection current
Radiation is faster at the top
questions.a: B) Cold air sinks, setting up a convection current. Cooled air is denser and sinks through the fridge.

questions.q: Answer the 4SD0-style question set on the equations, chloroplasts and uses of glucose.
questions.a: Marked with the mark scheme on the portal sheet
questions.model: Teacher answers Q1(a) on screen: balances the symbol equation step by step.

questions.q: Explain why a plant kept in the dark for two days loses mass. (3)
questions.a: No photosynthesis (1); it still respires (1), using stored glucose and starch (1)

questions.q: Explain why almost all food chains depend on photosynthesis. (3)
questions.a: Producers make glucose (1); energy stored passes to consumers when eaten (1); without producers no energy enters the chain (1)

questions.q: Explain why photosynthesis is described as endothermic. (2)
questions.a: It takes in energy (1) from light, which is stored as chemical energy in glucose (1)
questions.model: Two marks, two points: energy taken in (endothermic); where it goes (chemical store in glucose). Write both.
